newsitem.title: USA: V-ONE stock rises on U.S. export approval.
newsitem.headline: V-ONE stock rises on U.S. export approval.

text.p: V-ONE Corp's stock rose on Wednesday after the firm received permission from the U.S. Commerce Department to export computer encryption software.
In morning trading, the stock was up about 7/8 to 6-3/8, and about 37,600 shares had changed hands.
To get permission, V-ONE had to include a feature known as key recovery that allows the government to decode any message encrypted with the company's products, the firm told Reuters.
Encryption products, increasingly important for online commerce and global communications on the Internet, scramble information and render it unreadable without a password or software "key."

The Rockville, Maryland-based firm said its software, used to secure Internet communications, permitted the government to recover encryption keys without forcing customers to keep duplicates of their keys with a third party, as some other products require.

The export approval came under a new Clinton administration policy that took effect at the beginning of the year. Companies can export stronger encryption than previously allowed, but only if they incorporate key recovery features.
